newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank says German jobs market "gloomy".
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank says German jobs market "gloomy".

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Wednesday the overall picture in the German jobs market was gloomy in the first few months of 1997 amid a sharp rise in the number of people without work, particularly in construction.

The German central bank, in its monthly report for June, said the average number of working people in the first quarter on a seasonally-adjusted basis fell 0.7 percent to 34.05 million people from autumn 1996.
"The jobs market situation shows a gloomy picture overall at the start of 1997," the Bundesbank said.
The weak construction sector was largely to blame for the decline as many construction groups continued to lay off workers due to recessionary conditions in the industry.
In addition, the report said the service sector was failing to create new jobs due to regulatory barriers and wage costs.
The Bundesbank blamed structural factors for the ongoing high unemployment, which stood at an adjusted total of 4.36 million people, or 11.4 percent of the workforce, without work at the end of May.
The number of long-term unemployed, those without work for more than a year, had risen to about 31 percent of the total, which was about 1.2 million people, the central bank said.
Another one-fifth of the workforce was unemployed for between six months and one year.
The Bundesbank also noted some 1.5 million unemployed had no professional training and that 750,000 people could not take on full-time work for health reasons.
